propositions: Plan-review PASS verdicts must sign and persist a claim-valid attestation by default across all mutating public entry points (CLI and library), ensuring the claim gate can verify the review without a second LLM call.
Explicit unsigned execution requires a deliberate opt-out: --no-sign flag for CLI, sign=False parameter for library; omitting either should trigger signing.
BLOCK, INDETERMINATE, degraded, and local-source plan-review results must never be signed regardless of the opt-out setting, enforced at the shared attest.sign_plan_review seam.
Re-running a default plan-review operation with a current claim-valid attestation must reuse it idempotently without an LLM call or duplicate signature event.
A PASS whose signature persistence fails must return a retryable nonzero disposition and point to sign-review as the no-LLM recovery path.
CLI help and user documentation must clearly state the sign-by-default contract, name the explicit --no-sign exception, and document the sign-review recovery route.
